clusters.canonical_name: Windows Service-Based Persistence via SCM
clusters.rationale: Five notes converge on SCM-driven service creation/modification as unified persistence mechanism with SYSTEM context and reboot survival.
clusters.consolidated_description: Windows Service-based persistence via OpenSCManager, CreateService, and ChangeServiceConfig. Services survive reboot and run in SYSTEM context via the SCM. Entry point is SCM interaction; tradecraft includes service hiding via SDDL DACL manipulation.
clusters.priority_reason: 5 member notes, SYSTEM persistence, distinct from T-017's existing five-layer suite.

clusters.canonical_name: Port Monitor (AddMonitor) Persistence via Print Spooler
clusters.rationale: Five notes converge on AddMonitor as the API for registering malicious port monitor DLL into spoolsv.exe (SYSTEM context) on spooler restart.
clusters.consolidated_description: Port Monitor persistence via AddMonitor API and _MONITORINFO_2 structure. Malicious port monitor DLL loaded into spoolsv.exe with SYSTEM privileges on every spooler start. Survives reboot; distinct from service-based persistence and other T-017 layers.
clusters.priority_reason: 5 member notes, SYSTEM-context persistence, distinct print-spooler vector not covered in T-017.

clusters.canonical_name: AppInit_DLLs Registry Persistence
clusters.rationale: Three notes describe AppInit_DLLs registry key as distinct user32-linked DLL injection persistence mechanism with LoadAppInit_DLLs gating.
clusters.consolidated_description: AppInit_DLLs persistence via registry-resident HKCU/HKLM entry. DLLs loaded into all User32.dll-linked processes. Gated on LoadAppInit_DLLs registry value (admin required). Distinct from AppCert and RunOnce; user32-conditional loading profile differs from other registry persistence.
clusters.priority_reason: 3 member notes, clear user32-conditional tradecraft, registry-resident mechanism distinct from T-017 layers.

clusters.canonical_name: IFEO GlobalFlag and SilentProcessExit Registry Persistence
clusters.rationale: Eight notes converge on IFEO and GlobalFlag/SilentProcessExit as distinct persistence triggers: start-time redirect and exit-time recovery.
clusters.consolidated_description: IFEO persistence via Debugger key (redirects launches to malicious binary) and GlobalFlag/SilentProcessExit (executes recovery command on exit). Registry-resident under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options\<binary>. Admin/SYSTEM required; survives reboot.
clusters.priority_reason: 8 member notes (strong cross-source signal), two distinct persistence triggers, clear operational value.

clusters.canonical_name: WMI Permanent Event Subscription Persistence
clusters.rationale: Nine notes converge on WMI event subscriptions (__EventFilter + EventConsumer + FilterToConsumerBinding) as unified CIM-repository-resident persistence.
clusters.consolidated_description: WMI permanent event subscriptions via __EventFilter (event definition), CommandLineEventConsumer, and __FilterToConsumerBinding (association). Subscriptions survive reboots and execute within WmiPrvSE.exe context. Extrinsic events (polling) vs. intrinsic events (fire immediately) provide different triggering profiles.
clusters.priority_reason: 9 member notes (strongest signal), distinct CIM-repository mechanism, multiple event-trigger variants.

clusters.canonical_name: SERVICE_FAILURE_ACTIONS Crash-Triggered Persistence
clusters.rationale: Four notes converge on SERVICE_FAILURE_ACTIONS structure used with ChangeServiceConfig2 as distinct persistence executing on service failure.
clusters.consolidated_description: SERVICE_FAILURE_ACTIONS persistence via ChangeServiceConfig2 to execute recovery command when service fails. Operators force service failure to trigger recovery action. Survives reboot; SCM-monitored. Distinct from service-binary-modification persistence; provides fail-safe resilience.
clusters.priority_reason: 4 member notes, distinct SCM-native trigger mechanism, clear recovery/resilience purpose.

clusters.canonical_name: On-Disk Binary Patching for Persistence and Evasion
clusters.rationale: Three notes converge on in-place binary modification (code caves, import table patching) as persistence mechanism surviving reboot.
clusters.consolidated_description: Binary patching persistence via on-disk PE file modification: code-cave shellcode insertion, import-table patching, resource-section modification. Survives reboot (unlike in-memory unhooking); can target system DLLs. Persistence through modification of application logic at rest; evasion through modification of signature-scan targets.
clusters.priority_reason: 3 member notes, persistent (survives reboot), distinct from ImagePath-based service persistence.

clusters.canonical_name: SDDL/ACL Hardening for Persistence Resilience
clusters.rationale: Two notes describe SDDL strings and ACL manipulation to harden persistence objects against defender actions.
clusters.consolidated_description: SDDL and ACL hardening for persistence resilience via GetNamedSecurityInfo/SetNamedSecurityInfo/EXPLICIT_ACCESS_A. Operators deny stop and delete permissions to defenders, preventing removal of persistence objects. SDDL string format with ACE field decomposition provides the manipulation primitive.
clusters.priority_reason: 2 member notes, secondary persistence-hardening technique, overlaps with service hiding.

clusters.canonical_name: Service Hiding from SCM Enumeration
clusters.rationale: Three notes converge on using SDDL strings to hide services from SCM enumeration while maintaining SYSTEM access.
clusters.consolidated_description: Service hiding via SDDL string configuration that denies query rights to Interactive Users, Service Users, and Administrators while preserving SYSTEM access. Custom SDDL strings hide services from sc query and GUI enumeration. Complements service-based persistence by concealing the execution layer.
clusters.priority_reason: 3 member notes, distinct stealth mechanism complementing service persistence.

clusters.canonical_name: AppCert DLL Injection Persistence
clusters.rationale: Single note documents AppCertDlls registry mechanism as distinct DLL injection persistence vector triggered on CreateProcess-family API calls.
clusters.consolidated_description: AppCertDlls registry persistence that injects DLL into any process calling CreateProcess-family APIs or WinExec. Registry key: HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\AppCertDlls. DLL loaded whenever process spawns via documented creation APIs; host-activity triggered persistence.
clusters.priority_reason: Singleton, distinct from other T-017 persistence layers, narrow host-activity-triggered profile.

clusters.canonical_name: Heaven's Gate: 32-to-64-Bit Syscall Transition
clusters.rationale: Three notes describe 32-bit processes transitioning to 64-bit code space via ntdll Wow64Transition to issue native 64-bit syscalls.
clusters.consolidated_description: Heaven's Gate is a 32-bit-to-64-bit transition mechanism Wow64 processes use to issue native 64-bit syscalls. Entry via segment 0x33 jump through ntdll.Wow64Transition to wow64cpu.dll, then to 64-bit ntdll syscall stub. Allows 32-bit implants to bypass 32-bit ntdll hooks entirely while executing kernel-mode operations in 64-bit context.
clusters.priority_reason: 3 member notes, novel architecture bypass (32-bit implant issuing 64-bit syscalls), fills gap in T-001-T-006.

clusters.canonical_name: Manual GetProcAddress Implementation via Export Table Walking
clusters.rationale: Two notes converge on manually walking kernel32 IMAGE_EXPORT_DIRECTORY to implement GetProcAddress without userland API calls.
clusters.consolidated_description: Manual GetProcAddress implementation via direct export table walking using kernel32's IMAGE_EXPORT_DIRECTORY. Developers manually traverse AddressOfNames, AddressOfNameOrdinals, and AddressOfFunctions to resolve function addresses without calling Win32 API. Enables import-hiding and reduces EDR hook surface.
clusters.priority_reason: 2 member notes, distinct evasion primitive for import resolution, complements PEB-walker.

clusters.canonical_name: Sywshipers3: Random Syscall Dispatch via EGH
clusters.rationale: Single note describes Sywshipers3 as syscall-detection bypass using EGGs and random syscall jumps.
clusters.consolidated_description: Sywshipers3 is a syscall-detection bypass tool using EGG-hunter style stubs and random syscall jumps in Wow64 and x64. Distinguishes itself from deterministic SSN-based dispatch by using randomization to evade signature-based detection of specific syscall numbers. Focuses on evasion through indirection rather than architecture manipulation.
clusters.priority_reason: Singleton, narrow applicability (detection evasion), less-documented than SSN-based approaches.

clusters.canonical_name: Cross-Session Process Injection via WTS Enumeration
clusters.rationale: Three notes describe targeting variant using WTSEnumerateProcessesEx to identify and inject into processes in different logon sessions.
clusters.consolidated_description: Cross-session process injection via WTSEnumerateProcessesEx for identifying processes across multiple logon sessions. Operators enumerate session IDs and target high-value processes in other sessions (e.g., SYSTEM session from user session). Distinct operational variant from in-session injection; requires knowledge of session enumeration and cross-session process accessibility.
clusters.priority_reason: 3 member notes, distinct targeting criterion from core injection methods.

clusters.canonical_name: Manual PE Loader and Reflective DLL Injection (sRDI)
clusters.rationale: Three notes converge on manual x64 PE loader implementation including sRDI as position-independent variant.
clusters.consolidated_description: Manual PE loader for x64 executables with MZ header validation, section traversal, data directory processing, import/export table construction, base relocations, and entry-point dispatch. sRDI (Shellcode Reflective DLL) is position-independent loader variant providing custom helpers (GetProcAddressR). Bypasses userland APIs entirely with fine-grained relocation control.
clusters.priority_reason: 3 member notes, substantial SEC670 coverage, key infrastructure for manual code loading.

clusters.canonical_name: GUI Application Hook Injection via SetWindowsHookEx

clusters.consolidated_description: GUI application hook injection via SetWindowsHookEx to inject DLLs into processes that message-pump. Distinct from CreateRemoteThread-based injection; callback-based hook dispatch provides dedicated API surface for GUI targets. Requires message-loop presence in target; conditional on GUI application characteristics.
clusters.priority_reason: Singleton with GUI-specific applicability; narrower operational window than core injection.

clusters.canonical_name: Thread Context Hijack via CONTEXT Structure Modification
clusters.rationale: Single note establishes thread hijacking as distinct primitive focused on modifying thread's CONTEXT structure.
clusters.consolidated_description: Thread hijacking via direct CONTEXT structure modification using GetThreadContext/SetThreadContext. Requires appropriate handle access.
clusters.priority_reason: Singleton with focused applicability; overlaps with T-013 Remaining Methods.

clusters.canonical_name: Hook Trampoline Infrastructure for Non-Reentrant Hooks

clusters.consolidated_description: Hook trampoline infrastructure for implementing non-reentrant inline hooks. Enables both offensive (implant hooks) and defensive (unhooking) operations.
clusters.priority_reason: Singleton infrastructure primitive; secondary to primary injection techniques.

clusters.priority_reason: Singleton variant of process injection, overlaps with T-013 injection methods.

clusters.canonical_name: Custom Shell Loader as Distinct from Generic Injection

clusters.priority_reason: Singleton, foundational for API interception, enables post-exploitation capabilities.

clusters.canonical_name: Named Pipes for C2 Communication and Implant IPC

Supports network accessibility via Server service (\\ComputerName\pipe\PipeName). Named pipes offer duplex, network-capable communication vs. anonymous pipes (local-only, one-way). Provides kernel-mode transport with implicit buffering.
clusters.priority_reason: 3 member notes, distinct duplex transport mechanism, clear operational value.

clusters.canonical_name: Winsock Reverse Shell via Handle Redirection

Standard pattern for early-stage interactive shell establishing persistent socket-based I/O stream.

clusters.rationale: Single note documents full certificate pinning workflow for validating C2 server identity.

Implants validate server certificate chain offline to prevent MITM attacks and network-level redirection.

clusters.canonical_name: Token Theft (TokenThief) via OpenProcessToken and Duplication
clusters.rationale: Six notes converge on OpenProcessToken → DuplicateTokenEx → CreateProcessWithTokenW as canonical token theft escalation pattern.
clusters.consolidated_description: Token theft for privilege escalation via OpenProcessToken to obtain token from higher-integrity process, DuplicateTokenEx to create copy with MAXIMUM_ALLOWED rights, and CreateProcessWithTokenW to spawn child with stolen token's privilege level. Enables Admin-to-SYSTEM, High-IL-to-SYSTEM, and cross-privilege impersonation. SANS Lab 3.5 establishes as distinct offensive primitive.

clusters.canonical_name: SeBackupPrivilege / SeRestorePrivilege: ACL Bypass for File Access
clusters.rationale: Single note explicitly identifies SeBackupPrivilege and SeRestorePrivilege as privileges that bypass standard ACL checks entirely.
clusters.consolidated_description: SeBackupPrivilege and SeRestorePrivilege are special Windows privileges that bypass file DACL checks entirely, granting unrestricted read (Backup) or write (Restore) access. Any process with these privileges can access NTFS objects regardless of security descriptor. Operationally distinct from ACL manipulation; privilege-based bypasses. Often granted to backup operators, admins, or SYSTEM services; critical for sensitive file access (SAM, NTDS, DPAPI keys).
clusters.priority_reason: Novel capability, new territory for vault, critical for post-exploitation file access.

clusters.canonical_name: Token Privilege Abuse: SeDebugPrivilege and Privilege Manipulation
clusters.rationale: Single note covers coherent privilege-abuse tradecraft block: AdjustTokenPrivileges, SeDebugPrivilege, SeBackup/SeRestore, token stealing.
clusters.consolidated_description: Token privilege abuse via AdjustTokenPrivileges to enable privileges in current token (SeDebugPrivilege, SeBackupPrivilege, SeRestorePrivilege, SeImpersonatePrivilege). SeDebugPrivilege enables OpenProcess with high-privilege access; SeBackup/SeRestore bypass ACL checks; SeImpersonate enables token stealing. Integrated tradecraft covering privilege escalation via both OS-granted and privilege rights.
clusters.priority_reason: Singleton, covers coherent privilege-abuse family, broader than token theft, distinct from UAC bypass.

Pattern foundational for COM-hijack target discovery (T-017), autostart location enumeration, and registry-based inventory. Distinct from single-key lookups.

clusters.canonical_name: DPAPI Master Key Extraction for Credential Decryption
